correctness.rationale: A direct proof uses Gram determinants to exclude even common lines, uniquely parametrizes each LCD plane through an odd line by an odd vector in its orthogonal complement, and shows associatedness iff the two representative vectors have dot product one. The characteristic vector t+u has norm determined by n parity and gives the exact local edge counts; the unique intersection line prevents double counting. All n>=2 including n=2,3 are handled. Independent exact brute and line enumerations agree on overlapping ranges.

value.rationale: The 2025 primary conference slides explicitly identify counting associated-neighbor edges as proposed work. The theorem computes this natural graph invariant in the first nontrivial code dimension for every block length, separates parity regimes, and identifies the parity obstruction and characteristic-vector exceptional case. It is not a small finite table or a direct restatement of the ordinary-neighbor degree theorem.
